title: The End of the Express Road for Hybrid Vehicles: Can Governments’ Green Product Incentives Backfire?
authors: Cheng He; O. Cem Ozturk; Chris Gu; Jorge Silva‐Risso
eligible_reason: No qualifying linear staggered TWFE specification. Every Table 2-6 sales regression is a negative binomial model (SAS proc glimmix with a county random intercept, or proc genmod, link=log dist=negbin) with model x year x month and matching-strata x model effects plus time-varying controls (price, gasprice, fuelstation). The HOV-access termination is a single common date for the treated California counties (termination = 1 from May 2011 in the shipped data; Tables 2, 3, 5), so it is not staggered. The launch analysis (Table 4) pools California (Aug 2005) and other-state launches (2009-2010) with every effect interacted with a CA indicator, still negative binomial with controls. The only linear models (Table 6 carpooling, proc surveyreg carpool_pct_ln = strata year termination / treat launch) are single-state, single-date 2x2 designs on matching strata without county FE.
design_notes: County x vehicle-model x month sales panels around California's HOV-sticker termination for hybrids (2011) and HOV-incentive launches (CA 2005; other states 2009-2010), treated counties matched to control counties (strata from matching). Treatment variables: termination, launch. Estimation: SAS glimmix/genmod negbin with random county intercepts, controls pop income edu commute gasprice fuelstation unemployment male age price; heterogeneity columns add termination x county characteristics.
data_files_note: Code comment: 'due to the size of dataset, we select a random sub-sample of original dataset in the provided supplementary materials' (sample_green: 6,056 rows; sample_launch: 28,751 rows). Original data are J.D. Power PIN transactions (proprietary).
data_provenance_note: Random sub-sample of the proprietary J.D. Power data, per the code header; full estimation data not shipped.
software_notes: SAS (proc glimmix, proc genmod, proc surveyreg)
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available; screened from the SAS code (sas code.sas / code in text.txt), the shipped data, and the OpenAlex abstract. Adoption timing checked in the shipped data: termination first observed May 2011 in all treated counties (a handful of Mar/Apr 2011 rows). Nonlinear models with time-varying controls in every column, so not coded as a near miss.
